parts.title: The missing wallet
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last Saturday, I went into town to buy my mother a birthday present. I had saved sixty pounds for it, and I carried the money in a small brown wallet. I was feeling very pleased with myself as I walked down the high street.

In the third shop I visited, I found a beautiful scarf. When I went to pay, I put my hand in my pocket, but the wallet was not there. I checked the other pocket, and then my bag. Nothing. My face went hot, and the shop assistant looked at me kindly. 'Take your time,' she said.

I ran back to the two shops I had visited earlier, but nobody had seen it. Next, I went to the police station, where a policeman wrote down a description and told me to leave my phone number. I was almost in tears.

On Monday, a woman rang me. She had found the wallet in a bus shelter and had seen my name on a library card inside. Everything was still there, even the sixty pounds. I met her to say thank you and gave her a box of chocolates. Then I went back and bought the scarf.

questions.prompt: What was the writer's plan in town?
options: To buy a present for his mother
To visit friends in the library
To meet his mother in a café
questions.explanation: He went to buy his mother a birthday present.

questions.prompt: What did the writer discover in the third shop?
options: His bag had been cut open
questions.explanation: He put his hand in his pocket and the wallet was not there.

questions.prompt: How did the shop assistant react?
questions.explanation: She looked at him kindly and told him to take his time.

questions.prompt: What did the policeman do?
options: He gave the writer some money
He went to look for the wallet
He took a description of the wallet
questions.explanation: He wrote down a description and asked for a phone number.

questions.prompt: How did the story end?
questions.explanation: A woman had found the wallet and rang him.

parts.title: What to do if you lose something
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Everybody loses things from time to time. It might be a key, a phone or a bag. When it happens, the most important thing is to stay calm. [1] Panic makes it harder to think clearly, and you may forget something obvious.

Start by thinking about where you last had the item. [2] Walk the same route again and look carefully, because things are often found in places we have already looked.

If you lose something on public transport, contact the company straight away. [3] Many companies have a lost property office, and most of them have a website where you can fill in a form.

If you lose something valuable, like a passport, tell the police. [4] You will be given a number, which you may need later for insurance. [5] Finally, try not to blame yourself, since it happens to everyone.
sentences: They will make a note of the details in their report.
Staff may already have found it and be keeping it safe.
Take a deep breath and sit down for a moment.
It is also a good idea to ask friends to help you.
Perhaps you took it out of your pocket at the café.
Next time, write your phone number inside your bag.

gaps.explanation: Taking a deep breath matches staying calm, and panic is mentioned next.
Perhaps you took it out at the café continues thinking about where you last had it.
Staff may already have it, which leads to the lost property office.
They make a note in their report, and then you receive a number.
Writing a phone number inside is a final practical tip, with a closing thought.

parts.title: Information from the lost property office
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: agnes
turns.text: Hello, and thank you for calling the Central Lost Property Office. My name is Agnes. Our office is on Park Street, next to the post office. We are open from nine until one, Monday to Friday, and we are closed at weekends. When you visit, please bring your passport. You will also need to describe the missing item. The most common items we receive are umbrellas, followed by phones and gloves. We keep everything for thirty days. If you cannot visit us in person, you can send a friend with a letter from you. There is a small charge of three pounds for each item. To check if we have found something, please go to our website and look at the list.

gaps.explanation: Our office is on Park Street.

gaps.prompt: It is open from nine until ___

gaps.explanation: The most common items are umbrellas.
We keep everything for thirty days.

gaps.prompt: There is a charge of ___ pounds
gaps.explanation: A small charge of three pounds.

parts.title: A bus driver
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: My guest today is Ingrid Hale, who has been a bus driver for eleven years. Ingrid, what is the strangest thing that people have left on your bus?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: A parrot, in a cage. It sat on the back seat and shouted 'Hello!' at everyone getting on. Its owner came back the next day, very embarrassed.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: What items do people forget most often?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: Phones, definitely. People get off in a hurry and leave them on the seat. I probably find three or four a week.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: What do you do with them?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: I take them to the office at the end of my shift. If the phone rings, I answer it and say where it is.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: Have you ever had a difficult day?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: In winter, when it snowed heavily and the road was closed. I had thirty passengers who were late for work and very unhappy.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: What do you like most about the job?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: The people. I know the regular passengers, and we often chat. A boy I used to drive to school now rides my bus to university.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: Is there anything you would change?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: The early starts. I get up at four, and it is dark and cold. But I still love it, to be honest.
